exactness_argument: A normal-basis word v of GF(2^83) is an element of R = F2[X]/(X^83+1) and the Frobenius rotates it, i.e. multiplies it by a power of X. rotkey(v) = v^83 in R. Invariant: (X^s v)^83 = X^(83 s) v^83 = v^83. Complete: X^83+1 = (X+1) Phi_83 with coprime factors and Phi_83 irreducible over F2 (2 has order 82 mod 83: 2^41 = -1 mod 83), so R = F2 x F_{2^82}; v^83 = w^83 forces equal parity (a^83 = a in F2) and xi^83 = eta^83 in F_{2^82}, so xi = eta = 0 or xi/eta is an 83rd root of unity, and those are exactly the powers of X (order 83 in F_{2^82}^*); hence v = X^s w. So rotkey(v) = rotkey(w) iff lift_scan(v).0 = lift_scan(w).0, and the rotation-key table built from the compact table (key rotkey(c) for every stored canonical word c, the same packed value) is the same key -> value map: rotkey is injective on the stored canonical words, so no entry is merged or shadowed (the build reports compact entries - rotation-key entries, which the gate requires to be 0). The rotkey loop emits the frame loop's partner words in the frame loop's order (the same code) and looks up rotkey(partner) where the frame loop looks up lift_scan(partner).0, so every probe has the same hit status and, at a hit, the same packed value; the partner shift is then computed by lift_scan on the hit partner (the frame loop computed it for every partner), the hit is checked against the compact table (panic on a difference), and the frame loop's exact S3-order resolution, lift and relation check run unchanged. Hence the same first hit, lift, relation and probe count in every attempt, the same echelon and B's factor-log table. The definition of the probe count is unchanged: hits are resolved in the same order, so the probe-count identity is part of the gate, not an assumption. Tested: exhaustively at n = 11, 13, 19 (complete) and n = 7, 17 (2 not primitive: classes merge, the negative control); the carry-less kernel against the reference product and under rotation on random words; the rotation-key table against the compact table on every stored key of a 9-orbit base; the rotkey and rotkey_plant loops against the frame and S3 loops on 40 planted targets (both orders, folded and unfolded); and key by key against lift_scan and the compact table on every probe of every kKX rank stage.
gates: every scheduled row valid (exit 0, verified, schedule match, no memory event)

every IC process: lift_scan, Feistel, prefetch; the 16-byte compact table with 2^26 slots over the folded index (14,940,300 stored of 29,880,000 logical states); 29,878,182 table entries; logical-state blake3 and table-map digests equal B's (online.index_digest); no root bloom
per point: one scalar across every IC process (cold and rank) and rT, replayed as [d]G = Q in the pinned oracle
per point: one relation (point indices) and one probe count across every IC process on the point
Q0 (O1): cP and cK give the archived Feistel relation and scalar with 1,987,852 probes
rank arms: full rank, the arm's KIC_RANK_SOLVE recorded, and the written factor-log table equal to B's archived table, log for log

per rank block: rank_relations_blake3, the per-attempt probe vector (600 entries), rank_root_calls_total and the point-addition counters (rank_padd_fallback_states, rank_padd_irregular_inputs, rank_padd_resolved_hits, rank_padd_swapped_pairs) identical across kP, kK, kKaa and kKX (the candidate keeps every relation, every probe and every pair order of the baseline, not only the table)
frame counters: every rank arm builds exactly one frame per rank attempt; rank_frame_plant_checked_inputs and rank_padd_plant_checked_inputs are 0 everywhere

rotation-key counters: kP builds no rotation-key table and verifies and checks nothing; kK, kKaa and kKX build exactly one table, with rank_rotkey_compact_entries = rank_rotkey_table_entries = 29,878,182 (rank_rotkey_collisions 0: no two stored classes share a key), the pclmulqdq kernel, and at least one verified hit per attempt (every rotation-key hit is checked against the compact table in the producer, panic otherwise); rank_rotkey_hit_verifies identical across kK, kKaa and kKX per block; kKX has rank_rotkey_plant_checked_probes > 0 (every probe of its rank stage compared with lift_scan and the compact table) and kK / kKaa have 0
multiplicity: one primary statistic; every secondary is descriptive and never changes the verdict

question: Does keying the rank-probe producer's rank-stage probes by a rotation-invariant key (rotkey(v) = v^83 in F2[X]/(X^83+1), a complete invariant of the Frobenius rotation class of the normal-basis word, computed by 5 squarings and 3 multiplications with pclmulqdq) instead of the least rotation (lift_scan), with lift_scan run only at a table hit, lower the END-TO-END cold cost (setup + index build + rank stage + linear algebra + one-target online) of the rank-probe n=83 K600 producer on new targets and new rank seeds, with every rank relation, every per-attempt probe count, every scalar and the factor-log table unchanged?
